utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Whiting. This brings us to the end of your testimony, Mr. Plejo. Thank you very much for taking the time off to come and testify at the Tribunal. You are now excused. You may stand down. Thank you so much, once again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'd like us to deal with one or two housekeeping matters. I hope they will not take us beyond 7.00. Judge Hoepfel suggests we go into private session. I don't know. I was going to deal with something that happened in public session any way, open session any way. Anyway, can we go into private session, if that helps?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I was saying yesterday, the Chamber indicated that it was going to ask the supervisor of the interpreters to file a report, and a report has been duly filed. May it please be brought up on the screen? I must apologise, Mr. Milovancevic, we don't have it in B/C/S. May I ask the usher to please stand by the ELMO so that as people read it, it can -- you can scroll up? You can go up to show the very last sentence as well. Thank you. Are you done, Mr. Milovancevic? Thank you. Mr. Milovancevic, that is the report we have got. Do you have any comment to make?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have seen the report. I have no specific comment. Thank you. I believe we cleared up this question yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I understand that we cleared it up yesterday, Mr. Milovancevic, but the Chamber did say that it was going to ask for this report. Obviously you don't just get the report and do nothing about it. What I do want to find out from you is, do you have any reaction to this report or not? And if you do have, what is the reaction?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I see that the translator here acknowledges that there was a mistranslation, and I also accept that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. If you do accept that -- thank you very much, Mr. Milovancevic, that you do say you accept that. Let me just get clear. You do accept indeed that it was a mistake?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Okay. Thank you. I don't know whether anybody needs -- wants to say anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Not from us, no, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Judge?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: No, nothing I wish to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milovancevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we are about to call it a day. We are no longer dealing with this topic and I have no comment on that but I should just like to say this. We had estimated five hours as the time required for this witness, whom we have just finished. The examination lasted much longer than that. We envisaged three witnesses for this week, and we are concerned and should like to ask the Trial Chamber to bear this in mind when allotting the time to them, namely whether we have exceeded our previously allotted time or not, namely to take the situation into account.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Not quite sure I understand how you want to us take the situation into account. I just wasn't completely done with this report, Mr. Milovancevic. I just wanted to say about this report, as a final word, that if you do say you accept this, this report and its explanation, I am grateful to you for that. But I just want to note then that this therefore means that it brings this matter to closure. And I just wanted to say to you that I hope that it doesn't happen then again in the future that we make these allegations which can be very serious. And this was a very serious allegation when we are not absolutely sure of our facts. That's all I just wanted to say. And I don't think I want to elaborate on that, but if you want to say something?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I accept what you have said but I should like to voice my own hope that we won't be hearing any rooting comments from the interpreters booth which actually accounted for our reaction. I'm not only referring to this mistranslation now. Actually I should like to say that until last Friday we would not have reacted to such a mistranslation mistake, but after the incident, attention to which was drawn to us by Mr. Martic, we started to think about it in a different way. I wish to stress that we set great store by the integrity of this Tribunal and our own integrity and we do nothing in order to violate the rules or the order or to call in question the reputation of the Court. It was never on our mind. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic, you are opening a can of worms now. Last Friday, after you spoke to Mr. Martic, I specifically asked you what Mr. Martic had to say. And you said you would rather not talk about it. Now, it is known to you, you never put it on record, we don't know what it is, and you want us to accept that that is a reason for you behaving the way you behaved yesterday when we don't know what that is. You know, had you told us on Friday -- if you will listen to me it will be very helpful. Had you told us on Friday what Mr. Martic had said to you we would have attended to it immediately. Now you keep telling us, even yesterday you referred to this, that somebody said something, and we don't know what that thing is because you never reported it to us. And it makes it very difficult. Obviously, it is not as insignificant as you made it to appear on Friday. You made it appear very insignificant by saying no, don't worry, I don't want to talk about it. Now, suddenly it is becoming so significant that a week later, it still has an impact on how you behave. And even now, when we say we are closing this matter, you still put this as an explanation how, why you behaved the way you did. Obviously this is something that must have been very major and I can only regret that you didn't put it on the table. We are not able to address it because we don't know what it is. But enough said. I think people want to go home. It's a weekend now. Thank you so much. Just one last thing which I hope can be answered in one sentence. Do we know who is going to be testifying after the break? After the two- week break?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is the witness a witness who has been waiting here for two days now. He will return in two weeks. He will go back and return in two weeks. The colleagues from the Prosecution know who that is. Do you want me to tell you his name now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I don't know. Is it a protected witness? Is he a protected witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, he's not. It is Nikola Medakovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. I'm sorry to everybody for keeping you so long but this brings us to the end of the day today. We are going to take an adjournment and we are going to reconvene on the 9th of October. Now, I have not yet seen the scheduling for October so I am not able to see whether it's 9.00 in the morning or quarter past 2.00 in the afternoon and I'm not able to say in which court but it will be on the 9th of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Mr. Black, who is never wrong, says it's in the afternoon in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Black. What could this Chamber do without you, Mr. Black? Absolutely nothing. Thank you. There it goes. It's going to be in the afternoon at quarter past 2.00 in this courtroom. May the Court adjourn. See you on the 9th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 9th day of October, 2006, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.07 p.m.,
